connections.why: Units, uncertainties and graphing are first applied to describing motion
Acceleration from kinematics is linked to resultant force by Newton's second law
Newton's laws lead to conservation of momentum and the principle of moments
Force acting over a distance defines work and energy transfer
Work done stretching a material is stored as elastic strain energy
Upthrust and viscous drag are forces analysed with Newton's laws
Current and p.d. combine to define resistance and resistivity
Resistance values are combined to find circuit currents and power
Series ideas extend to potential dividers, e.m.f. and internal resistance
Conservation of momentum extends to impulse and two-dimensional collisions
Vectors and acceleration describe the centripetal motion of circular paths
Circular motion provides the mathematical framework for SHM
Orbital motion is circular motion driven by the gravitational central force
Charge and p.d. in circuits lead into capacitor charging and discharging
Electric and gravitational fields share the same inverse-square mathematics
Particle accelerators use magnetic forces to bend charged-particle paths
Wave properties combine through superposition to give interference and standing waves
Diffraction shows wave nature while the photoelectric effect shows particle nature
Photon and energy-level ideas underpin models of atomic structure
E=mc² links mass deficit to nuclear binding energy, fission and fusion
Nuclear stability and binding energy explain radioactive decay
Energy conservation extends to heating and phase change
Kinetic theory links molecular motion to internal energy and temperature
Black-body curves give the surface temperatures plotted on the H–R diagram
Gravity and orbital physics frame how stellar distances and luminosity are studied
Redshift applies the wave equation and Doppler effect to receding galaxies
